title: Global Drifter Program — Looper Trajectories
description: Looping NOAA drifter trajectories reveal persistent eddies and circulating ocean currents.
organization: NOAA Atlantic Oceanographic and Meteorological Laboratory
notes: North Atlantic subset with persistence over 100 days and up to 48 observations per drifter. ERDDAP's units row was removed for browser CSV ingestion.

title: IBTrACS North Atlantic tropical cyclone tracks
description: Atlantic tropical cyclone paths pair time, wind, and pressure observations across recent seasons.
organization: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
license: Full and open distribution with citation under the IBTrACS data usage policy
notes: Main-track rows for the 2011–2025 seasons, reduced to nine columns.

title: Natural Earth Admin 0 country boundaries — 1:50m
description: Query-ready country and territory geometries include centers, bounds, and approximate areas.
license: world-atlas ISC; source Natural Earth data is public domain
methodology: Converted vendored world-atlas TopoJSON to GeoJSON Polygon and MultiPolygon values. Added WGS84 bounds, spherical centroids, and approximate spherical areas.
caveats: Generalized visualization boundaries, not authoritative legal, cadastral, or maritime boundaries. Names and borders reflect the bundled Natural Earth edition.
notes: 241 country and territory rows with names, ISO numeric IDs, GeoJSON geometry, centers, bounds, and areas.

title: USGS magnitude 6+ earthquakes — 1900–present
description: A 126-year global record of strong earthquakes includes magnitude, depth, place, significance, and tsunami flags.
organization: U.S. Geological Survey Earthquake Hazards Program
license: USGS-authored data is in the U.S. public domain; attribution requested
methodology: Queried the USGS FDSN Event Web Service for all catalogued M6+ events from 1900 through the snapshot date.
caveats: Completeness and magnitude scales vary through time; catalog solutions may be revised after this snapshot.
notes: 14,517 global earthquakes with event links and tsunami indicators.

title: NOAA global historical tsunami sources
description: Tsunami source events span four millennia with cause, validity, wave height, intensity, deaths, and linked hazards.
organization: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information / World Data Service
license: Unrestricted and free online; cite NCEI/WDS Global Historical Tsunami Database, DOI 10.7289/V5PN93H7
methodology: Retrieved every published event through the HazEL API and normalized cause and validity codes.
caveats: Historical reports have uneven certainty and precision. Negative years represent BCE; filter validity for stricter analysis.
notes: 3,131 source events from 2000 BCE to the present.

title: NOAA global tsunami observations and runups
description: Observed wave locations connect coastal impacts and measurements to their originating tsunami events.
organization: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information / World Data Service
license: Unrestricted and free online; cite NCEI/WDS Global Historical Tsunami Database, DOI 10.7289/V5PN93H7
methodology: Retrieved every published runup through the HazEL API and retained event IDs for direct joins to tsunami_events.
caveats: Water-height reference levels and place precision vary among eyewitness, survey, gauge, and sensor records.
notes: 35,064 observations queryable by source event, date, location, distance, measurement type, and impact.

title: NOAA/SPC United States tornado tracks — 1950–2025
description: Seventy-six years of tornado paths pair start and end locations with intensity, dimensions, injuries, and fatalities.
license: U.S. federal government data; public domain with NOAA/SPC attribution requested
methodology: Expanded each SPC tornado record into one or two ordered path points; invalid 0,0 end coordinates were omitted.
caveats: United States only. Reporting practices and intensity scales changed over time; some early records lack valid end points.

title: Natural Earth major rivers and lake centerlines
description: Named world rivers and centerlines form query-ready ordered paths with display rank and zoom metadata.
methodology: Exploded named Natural Earth 1:50m line features at scaleranks 0–5 into ordered path points.
caveats: Generalized cartographic centerlines; not suitable for navigation, hydrology, or exact shoreline analysis.
notes: 16,820 ordered points describing major named river and lake-centerline segments.

title: Major theme parks and heritage landmarks
description: Well-documented theme parks and UNESCO-designated places provide a playful global point-of-interest layer.
methodology: Selected coordinate-bearing theme parks and UNESCO heritage-designated entities with at least 10 Wikidata sitelinks, then deduplicated by item and coordinate.
caveats: Sitelink count is a pragmatic notability proxy, not a quality or visitor-number ranking; some heritage entities represent cities or regions.
notes: 1,214 theme parks and heritage landmarks with Wikidata IDs and source links.

title: Global chain locations
description: High-confidence locations for eight familiar brands make global expansion, gaps, and geographic clustering easy to compare.
license: Overture Places CDLA Permissive 2.0 and documented source licenses; source data is not relicensed by Atlas
methodology: Selected open records at confidence 0.7 or above for eight Wikidata brand IDs, then assigned country names locally against the bundled Natural Earth polygons.
caveats: Overture Places can contain duplicates, junk, and incomplete properties. Generalized country boundaries can simplify disputed areas or leave near-border points unassigned.
notes: 31,313 locations across McDonald’s, Starbucks, KFC, Burger King, IKEA, 7-Eleven, Subway, and Domino’s.
